criteria: C1 Format: the reply parses as {answer, memories_used} JSON.
C2 Honest claims: every memory the model says it used was actually sent (validator drops nothing).
C3 Applied when it fits: every memory in should_use is listed as used.
C4 Not over-applied: no memory in should_not_use is listed as used.
_note: A case passes only if all four criteria hold. Cases marked replay=true are the three scripted demo prompts; replay mode runs only those. Criteria were written before the system prompt was tuned (Lecture 09: write the criteria first, then score).

cases.prompt: Can you suggest something I could make for dinner tonight?
I don't really understand how solar panels work. Can you explain it properly, step by step?
cases._why: Over-application case (Figure 1): a concise-summary preference from essay revision should not compress a requested step-by-step explanation.

cases.prompt: Can you write a birthday message for my best friend Sam? Something warm and a bit funny.
cases._why: Over-application case: a formal tone requested for an email to a manager should not be applied to a message to a friend.

cases.prompt: Write an email to my manager asking for Friday afternoon off.
Can you give me feedback on my essay intro? 'Computers changed the world. This essay is about the history of computers.'
What's a good recipe for a packed lunch?
Plan a dinner party menu for Saturday. I want to impress my guests and I have all afternoon to cook.
cases._why: Conflict case: the request overrides the stored weeknight time limit.

cases.prompt: Explain how a mortgage works in detail.
Write a thank-you text to my grandmother for the birthday gift she sent.
Summarise the plot of Hamlet in a few lines.
